summary: The recorded base reproduced the silent prompt_cache_key drop. The exact candidate preserves the field and forwards it into GenerateReqInput.cache_salt with native non-empty cache_salt precedence. Candidate regressions passed, and an independent real serving run produced cached_tokens 0/47/0/47 for identical A/A/B/B-keyed prompts, proving reuse within a key and isolation across keys.

tests.what_was_measured: At base 358c163250ad3b1f62939b01ce1314a0a31a0365, prompt_cache_key was silently absent from model_dump() and cache_salt remained null.

At candidate b747fb9ee118b07112396a58cb3873ee30145cfa, 61 focused protocol/adapter tests and 2 subtests passed, including field preservation, forwarding, precedence, absent-key, and empty-key boundaries.
Recreated the qualified deterministic two-layer tiny-Llama fixture outside the worktree with weight SHA256 6632fab7c351a0bd85518d80a89ec673f68139587f5ad3fa8d5ab38fad87e75f.
On one gfx950 GPU, four real /v1/responses requests with identical prompts and keys A/A/B/B returned HTTP 200 with cached_tokens 0/47/0/47.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) executed the deterministic tiny-Llama server under ROCm 7.2; the independent A/A/B/B serving probe observed cached_tokens 0/47/0/47.

remaining_limitations: No native C++, HIP, or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The available GPU was AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, not the reported NVIDIA RTX 5090.

The qualified random tiny-Llama fixture validates schema, HTTP transport, adapter forwarding, engine execution, and radix-cache namespace behavior only; it does not validate Qwen3.8-27B hybrid GDN behavior or semantic accuracy.
The reported 36,022-token latency measurements, 20-agent semantic-isolation workload, writable ten-tool workflow, and multi-node/distributed behavior were not reproduced.
The fixture tokenizer required a private minimal chat template for /v1/responses; generated weights and helper scripts remained outside the worktree.
